newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Coles sees higher annual net profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Coles sees higher annual net profit.

text.p: Australia's biggest retailer, Coles Myer Ltd, said on Wednesday it expected to report a rise in annual net profit with margins widening and a solid Christmas season already under its belt.
"This is very consistent with how we planned at the start of the year and we are very comfortable we are on plan," Coles Myer chief executive Dennis Eck told Reuters in an interview.
He declined to elaborate but confirmed he expected the group to post higher net earnings for the year ending July 27.
"Yes," he said. "That's a pretty safe question."

Coles earlier on Wednesday reported a 5.2 percent rise in second-quarter sales to A$5.5 billion, taking sales to A$9.945 billion for the first half ending January 26, an increase of 5.4 percent on the same period a year ago.
Eck said the group was trying to improve profit margins across all businesses and that Christmas trading showed margins could be repaired through better inventory management.
"We see that as we go along," he said.
Slim margins helped drag Coles Myer's profit 33.8 percent lower in 1995/96 (August-July) to A$280.4 million.
